about: What Lunenburg’s school buses cost, by year since FY2010: the school day against athletics, budgeted and spent; athletics by sport; and what the Dee Bus contract fixes through FY2028.

answer.text: Regular bus routes are under control, priced by contract to the dollar. The rest is less settled: special education busing keeps missing its budget, the bus fee has not lowered the town’s bus bill, and no one can yet say what each sport’s buses cost.

chains.label: Does not match
chains.question: Is special education busing budgeted right?

say.text: Special education buses spent $67,555 more than their FY2026 budget, and no transfer covered it.

link.label: Lines that closed the year past their revised budget

steps.text: Voted $565,734; $633,291 spent by the close of the year. No school bus line has run further past its budget in any year back to FY2010.

link.label: Lines that closed the year past their revised budget

steps.text: FY2027 budgets $649,953 for the line, $16,662 above what FY2026 spent. A Special Education Reserve Fund, accepted on 18 November 2025, exists for unbudgeted costs like this one.

link.label: Special education: budgeted above its spending for years, then below it

steps.text: It is not a one-off. From FY2017 to FY2022 the same line was budgeted $747,316 above what it spent; then it was cut, and it overran in FY2024 and FY2026.

link.label: Special education: budgeted above its spending for years, then below it

steps.text: A budget set from last year’s spending would miss in just this way; so would children’s placements changing after the budget is set. Nothing here tests either.

steps.closes: the special education van contract and a count of routes by year, from the district
steps.text: How many vans, monitors and routes the line pays for is not published, so a higher price cannot be told from more children carried.

chains.label: Matches
chains.question: Do the regular bus routes match the contract?

say.text: Regular bus routes now cost exactly what the Dee Bus contract says, and the FY2027 budget carries its price, $1,053,360, to the dollar.

link.label: Regular routes: the budget against the contract

steps.text: FY2025 spent its budget exactly, $907,200. FY2026 spent the contract’s first-year price exactly, $976,500.

link.label: Lines that closed the year past their revised budget

steps.text: Under the contract before this one the line overran: FY2023 by $29,925, and FY2024 by $49,925 even after $28,800 was moved in.
The price is fixed but not flat: it rises 7.9% into FY2027 and 7.4% into FY2028, against the 2.5% a levy may grow in a year without an override. The contract ends on 30 June 2028.

steps.closes: the Dee Bus contract that ran to June 2025, requested 9 October 2026
steps.text: The contract before this one has not been published, so neither why FY2024 cost more than FY2025 nor whether FY2026’s 7.6% rise was price or an extra bus can be told.

chains.label: Does not match
chains.question: Did the new bus fee lower what the town pays for buses?

say.text: No. In the bus fee’s first year the town’s general fund still paid the full $976,500 bus contract.

link.label: The bus fee and the general fund

steps.text: The Finance Committee was told the fee cut the line by $11,000. The line was voted at $965,500, and then $11,000 was moved back in during the year.

link.label: The bus fee and the general fund

steps.text: The only account named for a bus fee took in $52,717 in FY2026. It sits in the school choice fund, which spent nothing on buses and moved nothing to them.

steps.closes: the account the bus fee payments are deposited to, from the Town Accountant
steps.text: Whether that account holds the families’ fees at all is not established.

say.text: The FY2027 plan puts 83% of restored athletic buses back on the families’ fee fund, a year after the district moved them off it.

link.label: The FY2027 restoration: the plan against the sheet and the fund

steps.text: On 26 August 2026 the School Committee voted $10,000 from the town; the Superintendent put the rest, $50,000, on the athletic fee fund.

link.label: The athletic fee fund: receipts against spending

steps.text: Before the move the fund spent $284,723 more than it took in over FY2023 and FY2024, and the district said it could not carry the buses.

link.label: The athletic fee fund: receipts against spending

steps.text: After costs moved to the town line it took in $140,718 more than it spent over FY2025 and FY2026.

steps.closes: the athletic fee fund’s balance at each 30 June, from the Town Accountant
steps.text: Nothing published states what the fund holds after 30 June 2020, so whether it can carry $50,000 cannot be checked.

chains.label: Can’t tell yet
chains.question: Which sport’s buses cost most? Can we trust the figures?

say.text: Track, not soccer, costs the most to bus on the district’s sheet once its two split rows are added back together: $13,864 in FY2024.

steps.text: Boys’ and girls’ indoor track each print $6,931.75 for FY2024. Added, $13,863.50 is ahead of football’s $9,078.50 and girls’ soccer’s $7,662.00.
Outdoor track looks cheapest only in FY2025, whose spring section prints a $0.00 total and runs 46.1% below FY2024.
At the School Committee, members said the indoor track league meet had moved to the Reggie Lewis Center in Boston, and that the bus is billed in full while it waits there.
The contract bills every hour a bus waits: $130.00 an hour in FY2026, $140.00 in FY2027.

steps.closes: Dee Bus’s athletic invoices, each trip’s date, team, miles and hours waiting, from the Business Office
steps.text: The district’s second sheet prices FY2024 indoor track at $6,085.00, and no trip-by-trip record exists to say which sheet is right.

chains.label: Mixed picture
chains.question: Is the FY2027 bus budget as flat as it looks?

say.text: No. School-day buses rise 11.2% in FY2027; cutting athletic buses made the total look like 2.4%.

link.label: FY2027: the school-day rise under a flat-looking total

steps.text: Regular routes and special education go from $1,531,234 to $1,703,313. Athletic buses go from $127,550 to $0.

link.label: FY2027: the school-day rise under a flat-looking total

steps.text: The athletic cut offsets 74% of the school-day rise. The regular-route rise is the contract’s price; the special education rise is a budget, not a count.

link.label: The contract against this site’s model

steps.text: This site’s own model grows regular routes 6% a year and lands $14,828 under the price the contract already fixes for FY2028.

captions.said: The district told the Committee it pays Dee Bus for every hour a bus waits at an event, that track competitions run long, and that most of the charge is the waiting.
Members discussed indoor track: the league meet had moved to the Reggie Lewis Center in Boston, Lunenburg has no indoor facility of its own, and the bus is billed in full while it waits.
A bus taken to a track meet at the Reggie Lewis Center waits there most of the day; a van was raised as a cheaper way to carry a small group.

circuit_breaker.comment: Supplemental payment increased transport reimbursement to 75%.

conclusions.basis: MUNIS FY2026 year-end report, special education transportation (function 3300, object 535026): original appropriation, revised budget, expended and encumbered; the district’s FY2027 budget book, balanced scenario. Spent against the REVISED budget is the test of control; the FY2027 figure is set beside FY2026’s spending as a comparison, never as a projection.
conclusions.claim: Special education buses closed FY2026 $67,555 past their budget, and no transfer covered it.
conclusions.detail: Voted $565,734 and revised to $565,735; $620,025 paid out and $13,265 still committed at the close, $633,291 in all. FY2025 spent $434,922. The FY2027 balanced budget carries $649,953 for the line. The district’s FY2026 budget overview attributes the line’s growth to a 7% rate increase and more vans and monitors; that is its explanation, and nothing here tests it. The School Committee holds the line during the year; the Finance Committee weighs the next budget against it.
conclusions.not_shown: Why it overran. The van contract is not in the archive, so price, routes, children and monitors cannot be separated; the circuit breaker repays part of out-of-district transportation a year later and is never netted here.
conclusions.so_what: FY2027 budgets $16,662 above what FY2026 spent, after spending rose 45.6% in one year.

conclusions.basis: General fund special education transportation account, voted budget against spent at the close, every year: MUNIS year-end reports FY2023 to FY2026, the Finance Committee’s ledger history before that, tied to MUNIS where both exist.
conclusions.claim: From FY2017 to FY2022 the special education bus line was budgeted $747,316 above its spending.
conclusions.detail: It came in under its voted budget every year from FY2016 to FY2023, by $8,538 to $223,308; $348,067 of the gap in the window was FY2017 to FY2019, before the 2020 school closures. Against the voted budget it ran over by $65,455 in FY2024 and $67,557 in FY2026. The window is ours: it opens in the first year the gap passed $100,000 and closes in the year the budget was cut. What the data shows is a budget trailing its spending in both directions. Why is a hypothesis, untested: a budget set from the prior year’s actual would draw this shape, and so would placements arriving and leaving between budget and year.
conclusions.not_shown: Two of the window’s years are the 2020 and 2021 closures, when buses barely ran; the pre-closure part is given separately. How many children, vans and routes each year paid for is not published.
conclusions.so_what: Its FY2022 budget fell to $297,843, the lowest since FY2012; it then ran over in FY2024 and FY2026.

conclusions.basis: MUNIS FY2026 original appropriations; the district’s FY2027 budget book, balanced scenario, whose FY2026 column ties to MUNIS line by line.
conclusions.claim: FY2027’s school-day bus budget rises 11.2%; the transportation total rises only 2.4%.
conclusions.detail: Regular routes and special education were voted $1,531,234 for FY2026 and carry $1,703,313 in the FY2027 balanced budget. All four transportation lines go from $1,662,784 to $1,703,313, because athletic buses go to $0 and band trips from $4,000 to $0. Budget to budget throughout. The two lines that carry children to school are the ones rising.
conclusions.not_shown: A budget is not a cost: the regular-route rise is the contract’s second-year price, and the special education rise is a budget, not a measured change in routes or children.
conclusions.so_what: Cutting athletic buses, $127,550, offset 74% of the $172,079 school-day rise.

conclusions.basis: MUNIS FY2026 year-end report, account 535025: original appropriation, transfers, expended; the contract’s FY2026 price; Finance Committee minutes, 20 March 2025; MUNIS school special funds, fund 1308, every account, FY2023 to FY2026.
conclusions.claim: In the bus fee’s first year, the general fund still paid the full $976,500 bus contract.
conclusions.detail: FY2026 regular routes were voted at $965,500, $11,000 under the contract’s $976,500 — the amount the Finance Committee was told the fee cut — then $11,000 was transferred in and $976,500 spent. In the school choice fund (1308), account 437601, SCH. CHOICE BUS FEE, took in $50,628.44 in FY2025 and $52,717.04 in FY2026, $103,345.48 in two years. From FY2023 to FY2026 that fund has no expense account coded to transportation, and its transfer to the general fund is zero every year. Measured: the general fund paid the whole contract. A hypothesis: the fund 1308 receipts are the fees.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether the fund 1308 receipts are the fees is not established: the account is named for school choice. How many families paid is not published. What the fee was meant to fund is a question for the budget to answer.
conclusions.so_what: The fee’s candidate account took in $52,717; its fund spent nothing on buses. What does the fee pay for?

conclusions.basis: School Committee minutes, 26 August 2026, 12 March 2025 and 16 April 2025, each quotation re-read from the archive on every build; the district’s by-sport workbook; the general fund athletic transportation account.
conclusions.claim: The FY2027 plan puts 83% of restored athletic buses back on the athletic fee fund.
conclusions.detail: On 26 August 2026 the Superintendent put restoring high school buses at $58,880, rounded to $60,000: $10,000 from the town and $50,000 from the athletic revolving account. On 12 March 2025 a School Committee member said athletic transportation accounting “has been corrected from past practice that was done incorrectly”, and in April transfers moved costs charged to the revolving account onto the town line. In FY2024 the town line was $40,000 of $117,555 on the higher of the district’s two sheets, 34%; the FY2027 plan’s town share is 17%.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether Special Town Meeting funded the town’s share is not in the ledgers held yet. The 2025 statement concerned how costs were accounted for; whether the plan is the same practice is the question, not a finding.
conclusions.so_what: In March 2025, moving them off it was called a correction. Nothing published yet says which practice holds.

conclusions.basis: MUNIS school special funds year-end reports, fund 1301, FY2023 to FY2026: revenue rows against expended plus encumbered; the general fund athletic transportation account’s FY2025 transfer; the FY2026 budget overview.
conclusions.claim: The athletic fee fund spent $284,723 more than it took in over FY2023 and FY2024.
conclusions.detail: Receipts against spending, fund 1301: FY2023 $144,950 in, $314,864 out; FY2024 $135,765 in, $250,575 out; FY2025 $131,481 in, $32,796 out; FY2026 $188,944 in, $146,911 out. The district’s FY2026 budget overview says the “athletic revolving can not support these increased costs”, which fits the first two years. The surplus came after costs moved to the town line: $47,822 was transferred into the general fund athletic line in FY2025, and the fund’s high school salaries account closed that year at -$5,337, which is what a reclassification out looks like (our reading). No balance after FY2020 is published.
conclusions.not_shown: The fund’s balance at any 30 June since 2020 is not published, so whether it ran below zero is unknown. In FY2026 its purchase-of-service account spent about what it did in FY2024; what that bought is not itemised.

see.label: The athletics fee fund, line by line

conclusions.so_what: Over FY2025 and FY2026 it took in $140,718 more, after costs were reclassified off it. FY2027 draws $50,000.

conclusions.basis: The Dee Bus bid form (Exhibit E), every rate checked against its printed totals; the agreement’s term; the district’s FY2027 budget book; this site’s model as published (model.json: the transport rate and its starting amount). The model is OURS.
conclusions.claim: The signed bus contract rises 7.4% into FY2028; this site’s model grows the line 6%.
conclusions.detail: The contract fixes FY2028 regular routes at $1,131,390 for 11 buses, 180 days, after $1,053,360 in FY2027 — and the FY2027 budget carries that price to the dollar. The model starts from $1,053,360 and applies its default rate: $1,116,562. The contract ends 30 June 2028; two option years are priced at $1,189,800 and $1,284,984. Special education transportation is not in this line; the model grows it with special education.
conclusions.not_shown: The contract fixes a price per bus; it does not fix how many buses run, and the district may add or drop up to two a year at the same unit prices.
conclusions.so_what: That leaves the model’s FY2028 regular routes $14,828 under a price already fixed.

conclusions.basis: The district’s sport-by-sport workbook (records request, June 2026) and “Athletics Costs (1).xlsx” from the Finance Committee’s FY2026 budget files, matched sport by sport through a crosswalk that is ours; the general fund athletic transportation account.
conclusions.claim: The district’s two athletic bus sheets price the same FY2024 sports at $113,766 and $81,553.
conclusions.detail: The by-sport workbook (records request) and the Finance Committee’s copy of a second sheet both print transportation for 24 sports in FY2024; 10 agree to the cent and 14 do not. The widest: Outdoor Track, $7,674.00 in one and $1,989.00 in the other. The workbook’s total for every sport it lists is $117,555. Both are hand-assembled and neither is a ledger, so this page publishes the spread and picks neither.
conclusions.not_shown: Which figure is right. Paired sports carry identical figures in both sheets, so per-sport amounts are allocations, not measurements. No trip count is published for any year.
conclusions.so_what: Both are above the $40,000 town line. Nothing published says which sheet is right.

gaps.what: What the Dee Bus rates and fleet were in FY2025, so the 7.6% FY2026 increase can be split into price and buses
Where bus fee receipts are booked
Which of the three published per-sport athletics cost figures is correct
Whether a general fund athletics line is net of the revolving fund
How many athletic bus trips each sport took, and what each trip cost
Whether the school choice fund’s SCH. CHOICE BUS FEE account is where the student bus fees are booked
How many vans, monitors and routes special education transportation pays for, and at what rates
How many children ride the school buses, and how many pay the fee
Why DESE’s FY2025 transportation spending for Lunenburg differs from the town ledger
What the athletic fee fund held at each 30 June, FY2021 to FY2026
What the athletic fee fund’s high school purchase-of-service account paid for in FY2026
Why FY2024’s regular-route bus spending was higher than FY2025’s
Whether the FY2025 spring section of the district’s by-sport athletics workbook is complete

grain: DOLLARS, school general fund, the budget voted before the year beside what was spent at its close (expended plus still committed), FY2010 to FY2026; never added together. Per-sport dollars are the district’s hand-assembled sheets (stated). Every trip count is OUR ESTIMATE.
not_established: How many athletic bus trips any sport took, or what any one trip cost. Every trip figure here is dollars divided by the bid form’s own average trip.
The FY2025 Dee Bus rates and fleet, so whether FY2026’s 7.6% was price or a bus.
Where the student bus fees are booked; the school choice fund account named for a bus fee is a candidate, not an established destination.
What the special education van contract charges, and for how many vans, monitors and routes.
How many children ride the buses, or how many families paid the fee.
How much of athletic transportation the athletic fee fund paid in FY2025 and FY2026; it books transportation inside one purchase-of-service account with officials, uniforms and ice time.
Why DESE’s FY2025 transportation figure differs from the town ledger.
What the athletic fee fund held at any 30 June after 2020, so whether it ran below zero in FY2024, and what it holds as FY2027 draws on it.
What the fee fund’s high school purchase-of-service account paid for in FY2026, the year the general fund line was budgeted to carry athletic buses in full.
What made FY2024’s regular routes cost more than FY2025’s; both years ran under the contract before the current one, which is not held.
Why the special education line was budgeted above its spending for years and then below it; every explanation offered here is a hypothesis.

said.quote: it is a 3 year contract with tentative increases over the 3 years
said.why: The district bringing the Dee Bus bid to the Committee, before the contract was signed in May 2025.

said.quote: 7.6% increase in Dee Bus services 7% increase in vanpool for special education transportation
said.why: How the FY2026 increase was described to the Finance Committee: a percentage, with no fleet or rate beside it.

said.quote: The cost of athletic transportation is not up 200%. The way we are accounting for athletic transportation has been corrected from past practice that was done incorrectly.
said.why: A School Committee member’s explanation of the FY2026 athletic line. The by-sport workbook is consistent with it: the cost was already about three times the line in FY2024.

said.quote: The implementation of transportation fee reduced the student transportation line by $11,000.
said.why: The only statement in the record of how the new bus fee entered the budget. It is the same amount the FY2026 line was voted below the contract price.

said.quote: A fourth transfer to move funds to the athletic transportation, special detail, dues and fees and the high school after school stipends, this is the first phase move making monies available in the athletic portion of the budget. We can go back and reclassify expenses that had been charged against the revolving account.
said.why: The FY2025 transfer that took the athletic transportation line from its voted amount to what it spent: costs charged to the fee fund, moved onto the town line.

said.quote: We have received 1,074 bus requests, and have 494 unpaid at this time.
said.why: The only count of riders in the record, taken before the first fee year began. A request is not a rider and an unpaid request is not a refusal.

said.quote: Chris Menard asks for a copy of the bus contracts. The schools will be going out to bid for school buses in January.
said.why: Said in FY2024, the year the regular-route line ran furthest over its budget, and ten months before the bid this page reads.

said.quote: Chris Menard suggests the schools work on the contract as it is scheduled to be renewed in 2028.
said.why: A Finance Committee member pointing at the one transportation decision the town controls on a schedule: the contract ends on 30 June 2028.

said.quote: We will need to pay Dee Bus Company upfront and that cost is $731.50.
said.why: One trip, priced under the new contract: a class field trip. It sits inside the range this page’s per-trip estimate uses.

said.quote: All athletic transportation would be cut saving: $127,550.
said.why: The FY2027 balanced budget, as presented to the Finance Committee.

said.quote: The transportation for Middle-High Band would be reduced to $5,000.
said.why: The same presentation. The FY2027 balanced budget in the district’s book carries nothing for either band transportation line; the minute and the book differ, and the record here does not say which held.

said.quote: a more creative avenue for further conversation needs to be had about the athletic transportation
said.why: A parent at public comment, on the cut. The same meeting heard a student ask why teachers were being cut while athletic transportation was not yet.

said.quote: two buses will be necessary for transportation to away games
said.why: The football boosters, offering to pay for buses after the FY2027 cut.

said.quote: the private transportation waiver currently included in FinalForms, which allowed student-athletes to be transported privately while district transportation was unavailable
said.why: A parent’s question: with district buses cut, athletes were being driven privately under a signed waiver. The FY2026 athletic line had come in under its revised budget.

said.quote: the verified transportation cost was approximately $58,880, which she rounded to $60,000. Of that amount, $10,000 would come from the additional appropriation and $50,000 from the athletic revolving account.
said.why: The Superintendent’s plan to restore high school athletic buses for FY2027. She attributed the lower figure to scheduling competitions closer to Lunenburg, more home competitions, and estimating from actual schedules.

said.quote: $10,000 toward the restoration of high school athletic transportation, with additional transportation funding to come from the athletic revolving fund. Ms. Young seconded the motion. The motion passed, 3-0-1
said.why: The vote on the plan: the town’s share of restored athletic buses, and the rest from the athletic fee fund.
The FY2027 special education transportation budget as presented to the Finance Committee, four months before FY2026 closed past its revised budget.

said.quote: the reduced cost resulted from scheduling more competitions closer to Lunenburg, increasing home competitions, and using actual schedules and prior-year spring costs to obtain a more accurate transportation estimate
said.why: The Superintendent’s reasons for the restoration estimate, as minuted. They are her account of the figure; the page sets it beside the district’s own FY2025 sheet and the contract’s FY2027 rates without testing it.

said.quote: 75% reimbursement for FY25 out of district special education transportation costs through the circuit breaker program increased from 44%
said.why: The district’s account of the state’s change to the transportation half of the circuit breaker. The state’s own schedule shows the payment rising the same year.
